390	/** The raw subprocess spawn + timeout-kill + stdout/stderr capture (never rejects). */
391	function runChild(
392	  command: string,
393	  args: string[],
394	  projectDir: string,
395	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
396	  role: string,
397	  signal?: AbortSignal,
398	  timeoutMs?: number,
399	  onChildPid?: (pid: number) => void,
400	  onOutputActivity?: () => void,
401	): Promise<{ output: string; exitCode: number; stderr: string; timedOut?: boolean }> {
402	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
403	    // Already-aborted before we spawn → don't launch at all.
404	    if (signal?.aborted) {
405	      resolve({ output: '', exitCode: 1, stderr: 'aborted before start' });
406	      return;
407	    }
408	    let timedOut = false;
409	    // `detached: true` puts the child in its OWN process group so we can reap the
410	    // WHOLE tree on abort/timeout, not just the immediate child. In dev the spawn is
411	    // `node <tsx-cli> invoke-once.ts`, and the tsx CLI forks a worker (invoke-once,
412	    // which spawns the agent) — a single-PID kill hits only the wrapper and orphans
413	    // the agent (EI-40). Group-kill (`process.kill(-pid)`) takes out wrapper +
414	    // invoke-once + agent together. The new group is the child's alone, so it can
415	    // never signal the operator host (a different group).
416	    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd: projectDir, env, detached: true });
417	    // EI-85: surface the child OS pid so the caller can record it on the nursery
418	    // row — the reclaim sweep liveness-checks /proc/<pid> rather than blindly
419	    // reclaiming a stale-heartbeat row whose child is actually still alive.
420	    if (child.pid != null) {
421	      try { onChildPid?.(child.pid); } catch { /* recording is best-effort */ }
422	    }
423	    let stdout = '';
424	    let stderr = '';
425	    let killGrace: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
426	    let aborted = false;
427	    // Kill the child's whole process group; fall back to a single-PID kill if the
428	    // group send fails (e.g. the child already exited / no group).
429	    const killTree = (sigName: NodeJS.Signals) => {
430	      const pid = child.pid;
431	      if (pid) { try { process.kill(-pid, sigName); return; } catch { /* fall through */ } }
432	      try { child.kill(sigName); } catch { /* ignore */ }
433	    };
434	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
435	      timedOut = true;
436	      killTree('SIGTERM');
437	    }, timeoutMs ?? invokeTimeoutMs());
438	    // Caller-driven abort (EI-40: fleet:cancel of an operator spawn): SIGTERM the
439	    // tree now, SIGKILL it after a grace period if it ignores the term.
440	    const onAbort = () => {
441	      aborted = true;
442	      killTree('SIGTERM');
443	      killGrace = setTimeout(() => { killTree('SIGKILL'); }, KILL_GRACE_MS);
444	    };
445	    if (signal) signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
446	    const cleanup = () => {
447	      clearTimeout(timer);
448	      if (killGrace) clearTimeout(killGrace);
449	      if (signal) signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
450	    };
451	    // P-008: every emitted chunk is the mid-turn signal — stderr counts too
452	    // (some backends log progress there while stdout buffers).
453	    const reportActivity = () => { try { onOutputActivity?.(); } catch { /* best-effort */ } };
454	    child.stdout?.on('data', (d) => { reportActivity(); stdout += String(d); });
455	    child.stderr?.on('data', (d) => { reportActivity(); stderr += String(d); });
456	    child.on('close', (code) => {
457	      cleanup();
458	      // A child we aborted may exit 0 (it caught SIGTERM and shut down) or via the
459	      // signal — normalize to a non-zero "aborted" outcome so callers don't read a
460	      // cancelled run as a clean success.
461	      if (aborted) {
462	        resolve({ output: extractAgentOutput(stdout), exitCode: 1, stderr: stderr.trim() || 'aborted (fleet:cancel)' });
463	        return;
464	      }
465	      const exitCode = code ?? 1;
466	      const failLog = formatInvokeStderr(role, exitCode, stderr);
467	      if (failLog) console.error(failLog);
468	      // A non-zero exit with EMPTY stderr is otherwise completely silent (the
469	      // upstream "exit=1 empty=true" hides whether the agent even produced output).
470	      else if (exitCode !== 0) {
471	        const dbg =
472	          process.env.PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_DEBUG === '1'
473	            ? `\n--- stdout tail (${role}) ---\n${stdout.length > 2000 ? stdout.slice(-2000) : stdout}`
474	            : '';
475	        console.error(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} exited ${exitCode} with empty stderr (stdout ${stdout.length} chars)${dbg}`);
476	      } else if (stderr.trim()) {
477	        // Exit 0 with non-empty stderr: surface it so the operator log shows why
478	        // the bee vanished (e.g. "You've hit your session limit"). Without this,
479	        // exit-0 runs are completely silent even when the stderr carries the cause.
480	        const stderrHead = stderr.trim().slice(0, 500);
481	        console.warn(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} exited 0 with stderr (${stderr.length} chars): ${stderrHead}`);
482	      }
483	      resolve({ output: extractAgentOutput(stdout), exitCode, stderr, timedOut });
484	    });
485	    child.on('error', (err) => {
486	      cleanup();
487	      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
488	      console.error(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} spawn error: ${msg}`);
489	      resolve({ output: '', exitCode: 1, stderr: msg });
490	    });
491	  });
492	}
